body: The conflict produced by this change is huge, even after applying the same change in my PR and cherry-picking your commit it doesn't show that the changes are just made for 2 lines only.
I can do away with the indentation change, no worries.

I tested the changes and they work as expected on top of my PR. However, the fix for [#42809](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/42809)
 affects all integer properties across the editor and project settings, and also removes the option to restore the up/down arrows when needed. It would be better to move this fix into a separate PR since it introduces a broader behavior change that likely needs its own discussion.

Here, there are projects that uses `hide_slider` hint string either while using the annotation `@export_range` or inside `_validate_property` method.

The complication comes from the approach taken, which could have been avoided by simply adding one more hint and a variable to control whether sliders are used for integer properties (with no effect on float properties). That way, we could also document that it’s possible to hide the up/down arrows for integer variables and show a slider instead using the `use_slider` hint string, and still hide the slider for both integer and float properties using `hide_slider`.

I don't quite understand the problem here? As I said, "hide_slider" still works, so compatibility isn't broken.

The new hint to always use sliders is "prefer_slider", which can be overridden if used with "hide_control"/"hide_slider".

Oh, you didn't remove the hint ? so `hide_slider` and `hide_control` are the same for float properties then, and it's more confusing now, we already can hide slider for float properties using `hide_slider` and we hide the arrows after this change using both `prefer_slider` and `hide_slider` together for integer properties, so why do we need `hide_control` then ?

Here's how it works:
- "prefer_slider": Makes integer values use the slider instead of the up-down arrows.
- "hide_control": Hides whatever is being used, either the slider or the arrows.
- "hide_slider": Same as above, but internally deprecated. Since its function is to hide not just the slider, but also the arrows, renaming "slider" to "control" makes more sense.

 			Hints that an [int] or [float] property should be within a range specified via the hint string [code]"min,max"[/code] or [code]"min,max,step"[/code]. The hint string can optionally include [code]"or_greater"[/code] and/or [code]"or_less"[/code] to allow manual input going respectively above the max or below the min values.
 			[b]Example:[/b] [code]"-360,360,1,or_greater,or_less"[/code].
-			Additionally, other keywords can be included: [code]"exp"[/code] for exponential range editing, [code]"radians_as_degrees"[/code] for editing radian angles in degrees (the range values are also in degrees), [code]"degrees"[/code] to hint at an angle and [code]"hide_slider"[/code] to hide the slider.
+			Additionally, other keywords can be included: [code]"exp"[/code] for exponential range editing, [code]"radians_as_degrees"[/code] for editing radian angles in degrees (the range values are also in degrees), [code]"degrees"[/code] to hint at an angle, [code]"prefer_slider"[/code] to show the slider for integers, and [code]"hide_control"[/code] to hide the slider or up-down arrows.
body: This should also be mentioned in `@export_range` description.

Step `0` seems not supported for integer properties.
 I didn't test this particular case, but it's likely broken.
You could add a check for `is_inside_tree()`, as this will be updated anyway in `NOTIFICATION_ENTER_TREE`.
tbh this could be a bitmask `SHOW_SLIDER | SHOW_ARROWS`, and you could use either, both or neither for both int and float. Currently it's a bit awkward. But that would require more changes.
